title: Handover
description: The body of the signed POST /v1/dispatches/<dispatch_id>/handover, application/json: the adapter that serves the node pool asks for the run key and the input of the job it started for the dispatch. Before calling handover, the adapter has satisfied itself that the job asking is the one it started for this dispatch. It passes the run key to that job alone, and keeps it no longer than that. How it proves the job is the adapter's business. A run key is handed over at most once per run: the answer, handover-answer.schema.json, is given once, sent with Cache-Control: no-store and never cached, and a second handover is refused, 409 handed_over. Once its handover is answered, a dispatch never goes back to the queue: a release after it ends the run, release.schema.json. A dispatch_id that is unknown, or that belongs to another adapter, is refused 403 forbidden, with the same signed body as an unknown pool, so nobody learns whether an id exists; the control plane decides this before any 409 or 410. The adapter's signature and that check authorise the request, not the id. A handover before dispatched is refused, 409 not_dispatched; after the lease lapsed and the dispatch went back to the queue with the same run, 409 lease_expired, and the adapter then stops the job it started for that dispatch; after the dispatch ended because its work item was closed or undone, 410 gone. It is signed with the adapter's access key as https://qory.dev/contracts/integration/v1/definitions.schema.json describes. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, or a request whose signature it has already seen, with an unsigned 401. A member this schema does not define is refused, invalid_request.

version.description: The document format. The control plane refuses a version it does not read.

time.description: When the adapter built the body, RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds. The control plane refuses a time more than 300 seconds from its clock, either way, with an unsigned 401.
